content.title: Meet The Ambassador: Lee Calcote, Layer5
content.summary: A conversation with Lee Calcote, founder of Layer5 and CNCF ambassador, exploring how community ambassadors promote service mesh adoption, open source collaboration, and best practices for Kubernetes users.

content.title: Meet the Maintainer: Linkerd
content.author: Thomas Rampelberg
content.summary: An overview of Linkerd, the CNCF service mesh project, presented by maintainer Thomas Rampelberg. The session highlights Linkerd's features, benefits, and ecosystem relevance for Kubernetes users seeking lightweight, secure, and observable service-to-service communication.

content.title: Meet the Ambassador: Gianluca Arbezzano, Influxdata
content.summary: This session introduces Gianluca Arbezzano, an InfluxData ambassador, highlighting his contributions to the Kubernetes community and discussing how InfluxDB and related tools enhance observability for Kubernetes users.

content.title: Meet the Maintainer: Kubernetes
content.author: Paris Pittman
content.summary: An overview of the Kubernetes project presented by a core maintainer, covering the core architecture, recent and upcoming changes, contribution pathways, and why understanding the project's direction matters to users and operators.

content.title: Building Images Efficiently and Securely on Kubernetes with BuildKit
content.author: Akihiro Suda
content.summary: The session explains how to run BuildKit on Kubernetes to build container images efficiently and securely, covering load‑balancing, distributed caching, rootless mode, secret management, and integrations with Buildpacks and Knative.
content.description: BuildKit is a modern container image builder that focuses on efficiency and security, mostly known as the backend of Docker 18.06+ and Jessie Frazelle's `img`. (But it is even useful as a standalone tool!) In this talk, Akihiro Suda, one of founding maintainers of BuildKit, shows practical tips for running BuildKit on Kubernetes clusters. His talk will contain: * Quick introduction to BuildKit * Why you should build images on your Kubernetes cluster * Load balancing and distributed caching * Dep

content.title: Kubernetes Security and How to Fix K8s Cluster at Scale
content.author: Simon Pearce
content.summary: The session details how a hosting provider secures and scalably upgrades multiple customer‑run Kubernetes clusters, illustrating the process with a real API bug fix applied across all clusters.
content.description: As a hosting provider, we have the challenge to run and manage multiple Kubernetes clusters for various customers on our infrastructure, similar to e.g. Google or Azure in a secure way. The majority of these clusters are fully managed by us. Our customers want to build and run containers. Not maintain and upgrade Kubernetes clusters. In this talk, we will give you a breakdown on how we help our customers to secure their clusters and how we can force Kubernetes upgrades to all clusters in a scala

content.title: Rootless, Reproducible, and Hermetic: Secure Container Build Showdown
content.author: Andrew Martin
content.summary: The session examines rootless container image build tools—such as BuildKit, buildah, Kaniko, and Makisu—focusing on security, reproducibility, and hermetic isolation to prevent privilege escalation in CI pipelines, and compares their strengths and weaknesses.
content.description: Rootless container image builds (as distinct from rootless runtimes) have crept ever closer with orca-build, BuildKit, and img proving the concept. And they are desperately needed: a build pipeline with an exposed Docker socket can be used by an attacker to escalate privilege - and is probably a backdoor into most Kubernetes-based CI build farms. content.title: Network Machinery: A United-Front for Network Troubleshooting with CRDs
content.author: Adel Zaalouk
content.summary: The session introduces a set of custom resource definitions (CRDs) collectively called NetworkMachinery to simplify and standardize network troubleshooting in Kubernetes, providing performance, debugging, and simulation tests for operators.
content.description: The current state of network troubleshooting in Kubernetes is complicated. The knowledge of how to troubleshoot Kubernetes networking is scattered all over the place either in the heads of highly skilled network crafts-men or as a tool that has its own learning curve and usually forged at a time of disaster in a fire-and-forget fashion. The goal of this talk is to propose and introduce a rather simpler way of pooling this common knowledge and tooling together into a well-defined, consistent and

content.title: Intro: Autoscaling SIG
content.author: Marcin Wielgus
content.summary: An introductory session on the Kubernetes Autoscaling SIG that explains the three autoscaling mechanisms—horizontal pod, vertical pod, and cluster autoscaling—how they work, when to use each, and how they complement each other.
content.description: Join members of SIG Autoscaling to learn how to automatically adjust your Kubernetes cluster and pods to match your current capacity needs. We'll discuss all available types of autoscaling - horizontal, vertical, and cluster. We will also explain ways to use them, when they are applicable and how they fit together.

content.title: Intro: CNCF CI
content.author: Lucina Stricko & Denver Williams
content.summary: The session introduces the CNCF CI status dashboard (cncf.ci), which continuously validates builds, deployments, and end‑to‑end tests for CNCF projects on bare‑metal Kubernetes clusters, providing visibility into CI health for the community.
content.description: The new and improved CNCF CI status dashboard -- cncf.ci -- provides a third party validation of builds, deployments and end-to-end testing for CNCF’s Graduated and Incubating projects. The CNCF CI status dashboard continually validates each CNCF project, for any commit on stable and head, running on Kubernetes clusters which are provisioned to a bare metal environment. The results of each testing stage are published to the cncf.ci status dashboard. An Intro session will give an overview of the

content.title: Intro: Cortex
content.author: Tom Wilkie
content.summary: The session introduces Cortex, a CNCF sandbox project that provides horizontally scalable, highly available, multi-tenant long‑term storage for Prometheus metrics and a Prometheus‑compatible query API, helping operators preserve metrics indefinitely and query them at scale.
content.description: Cortex provides horizontally scalable, highly available, multi-tenant, long term storage for Prometheus metrics, and a horizontally scalable, Prometheus-compatible query API. Cortex allows users to deploy a centralised, globally aggregated view of all their Prometheus instances, storing data indefinitely. In this talk we will discuss a bit of Cortex's history, Cortex's architecture and how to get started with Cortex. Cortex is a CNCF sandbox project.

content.title: Intro: Kubernetes (Release) SIG
content.author: Tim Pepper
content.summary: The session introduces the SIG Release and its Release Team, explaining how volunteers manage Kubernetes’s quarterly release cadence, the release process, roles, and opportunities for community involvement. It highlights how this work ensures reliable, high‑quality Kubernetes releases for users and operators.
content.description: SIG Release and the Release Team are looking for volunteers! This session will feature past and current release team members describing what the Release Team does: We will discuss how Kubernetes project volunteers manage the quarterly release cadence of the project, give an overview of the release process, release team roles, and how these support the SIG Release goal of producing high quality Kubernetes releases on a reliable schedule. We will highlight the opportunities for both new and experi

content.title: Intro: Kubernetes WG for Multitenancy

links.reason: The session introduces the Kubernetes Multi-tenancy Working Group, which focuses on soft and hard multi-tenancy. One of the core KEPs the WG is developing is KEP-1687 (Hierarchical Namespace Controller As A Subproject), which directly addresses multi-tenancy via hierarchical namespaces. The session explicitly mentions reviewing relevant KEPs from the WG, making KEP-1687 a specific match.

content.author: Tasha Drew
content.summary: An overview of the Kubernetes Multi-tenancy Working Group’s efforts, defining soft and hard multi-tenancy, outlining its project plan, and showing how newcomers can contribute while reviewing relevant KEPs.
content.description: This presentation will be an overview of the work the multitenancy group has been doing, defining soft and hard multitenancy and reviewing the project plan for addressing both that the working group is putting forward. We will explain how people new to the working group can get engaged and review the various KEPs that the working group is involved with.

content.title: Intro: Service Catalog SIG

links.reason: The session is an introductory deep‑dive into the Kubernetes Service Catalog project, which implements the Open Service Broker API. KEP‑706 specifically defines Portable Service Definitions for the Service Catalog, making it the relevant KEP for this implementation discussion.

content.author: Jonathan Berkhahn
content.summary: An introductory deep-dive into the Kubernetes Service Catalog project, showing how to provision cloud services via the Open Service Broker API and demonstrating a database provisioning workflow within a cluster.
content.description: This is an introduction to the Kubernetes Service Catalog project. Service Catalog lets you provision cloud services, regardless of where they are hosted, directly from the comfort of native Kubernetes tooling. This works across platforms because we follow the Open Service Broker API, an open standard to provision and manage cloud services. Learn how you can use Service Catalog to access third-party services from your Kubernetes applications. We will walk through provisioning a database directly

content.title: From Snowflake Servers to Snowflake Clusters - The GitOps Journey
content.author: Allison Richardet
content.summary: MasterCard shares its journey of moving from individual, manually managed clusters to a standardized, GitOps‑driven deployment model, highlighting how they tackled security, observability, and complexity while avoiding snowflake clusters.
content.description: At MasterCard, we have a unique hard requirement of one dedicated cluster per application due to security and other challenges. In an effort to prevent snowflake clusters, we provided a base set of services for logging, monitoring, etc.; however, application teams inevitably want to customize their logging solution or add a monitoring dashboard. We realized this mix of standard and optional services could quickly get out of control and needed normalization. In early 2018, we exposed application

content.title: P2P Docker Image Distribution in Hybrid Cloud Environment with Kraken
content.author: Yiran Wang & Cody Gibb
content.summary: The session presents Uber’s Kraken, a peer‑to‑peer Docker registry that leverages a BitTorrent‑like protocol to dramatically speed up large‑scale image distribution across multi‑zone, hybrid‑cloud environments, addressing performance and scalability challenges for Kubernetes operators.
content.description: Docker image is a foundational building block of container based infrastructure, but distributing high volume of docker images in a multi-zone, hybrid cloud system has been a scaling problem for many.In this talk, we will walk through different approaches we investigated for distributing docker images and introduce Uber’s own solution, Kraken, a P2P docker registry loosely based on BitTorrent protocol, and capable of distributing terabytes of images within seconds.This talk will cover:- Image di

content.title: Envoy SDS: Fortifying Istio Security
content.author: Yonggang Liu & Quanjie Lin
content.summary: The session explains how Istio’s Citadel Agent uses Envoy’s Secret Discovery Service (SDS) to dynamically provision X.509 certificates and keys directly to workloads, enhancing security by keeping private keys on the node and supporting both Kubernetes and VM workloads.
content.description: In Istio 1.1, Citadel Agent is introduced to dynamically provision x.509 certificates and private keys to workloads through the Envoy Secret Discovery Service (SDS) API. Running on Kubernetes nodes as DaemonSets and standalone on VMs, Citadel Agents improve security by making sure the generated private keys never leave the node and can be securely delivered to workloads via UDS. content.title: Istio, We Have a Problem! Understanding and Fixing Bugs with a Service-Mesh
content.author: David Gageot
content.summary: This session walks through using Istio’s service mesh to observe, debug, and fix issues in a micro‑service deployment, then demonstrates a non‑trivial blue‑green rollout with traffic mirroring, leveraging the Service Graph, Prometheus, and Grafana.
content.description: Istio, we have a problem! We've just deployed a shinny new set of micro-services and it behaves in a strange manner. Hard to say why with so many moving parts... Let's leverage the newly installed service mesh to understand what we've deployed, find the root problem, fix it with a bandaid and then do a proper, non trivial, blue-green deployment of a v2. That will involve the Service Graph, Prometheus monitoring, Grafana Dashboards, Traffic mirroring, all orchestrated in a simple manner by Istio.

content.title: Meet the Maintainer: Fluent Bit
content.author: Eduardo Silva
content.summary: An overview of Fluent Bit, the lightweight log processor and forwarder, its role in Kubernetes logging pipelines, and how operators can deploy and configure it for efficient container log collection and forwarding.

content.title: Meet the Maintainer: NATS
content.author: Waldemar Quevedo Salinas
content.summary: In this Meet the Maintainer session, the NATS project lead introduces NATS as a lightweight, high‑performance messaging system, explains its architecture and how it runs natively on Kubernetes using operators and Helm, and shows why it matters for building resilient, cloud‑native applications.

content.title: Databases on Kubernetes Using a Custom Operator: Day 1, Day 2, and Beyond

links.reason: The session focuses on building a custom operator that defines a new CustomResourceDefinition (CRD) to manage Neo4j clusters, describing the controller tooling and CRD implementation. This directly relates to KEP-95, which graduates CustomResourceDefinitions to GA and covers the Kubernetes implementation of CRDs.

content.author: Johannes Unterstein
content.summary: This case‑study walks through building and operating a custom Kubernetes operator for managing Neo4j database clusters, covering both day‑1 tasks like provisioning and day‑2 concerns such as rolling upgrades, backup/restore, and continuous deployment. It shows how operators can provide reliable, zero‑downtime DBaaS on Kubernetes.
content.description: We started the journey of building a managed cloud version of the graph database Neo4j. A bit later we started developing an operator to manage multiple database clusters in k8s.Handling persistence and Neo4j's own distributed consensus algorithm within k8s gave us a challenge. In this session we want to share the lessons we learned writing this operator and using it in production.We will start with how to get started using the k8s controller tooling to create an operator to manage a CRD. content.title: Unit Testing Your Kubernetes Configurations Using Open Policy Agent
content.author: Gareth Rushgrove
content.summary: The session explains how to use Open Policy Agent (OPA) to write unit tests for Kubernetes configuration files, enabling early detection of policy violations and integrating those tests into CI pipelines. It covers OPA's Regula language and how to apply testing across tools like Helm, Kustomize, and Pulumi.
content.description: Open Policy Agent provides a high-level declarative language to author and enforce policies on structured data, for instance Kubernetes configurations. OPA is typically used as a service to enforce authorization policy in a cluster. New configurations submitted to an API are filtered through OPA and accepted or rejected depending on the defined policy. content.title: Writing kubectl Plugins for Everyone: Develop, Package & Distribute

links.reason: The session focuses on the modern kubectl plugin framework, covering development, packaging, and distribution of custom kubectl subcommands, which aligns directly with KEP-2379 that defines and implements kubectl plugins.

content.author: Ahmet Alp Balkan
content.summary: The session explains the modern kubectl plugin framework, showing how developers can create, package, and distribute custom kubectl subcommands, empowering the community to extend kubectl without altering core code.
content.description: Many users install extra tools for tasks they can't do with kubectl. Did you know you can write and distribute your own kubectl subcommands? kubectl had notion of plugins since 2016, but after listening to the community feedback, SIG CLI revisited the idea, and new and simpler plugin mechanism is now available in kubectl. content.title: Intro: Azure SIG
content.author: Stephen Augustus
content.summary: An introductory session on SIG Azure covering its purpose, recent work across Kubernetes 1.14‑1.15 and upcoming 1.16 features, user stories of running Kubernetes on Azure, and ways for the community to get involved.
content.description: In the SIG Azure Intro, we’re going to tell you all about why SIG Azure exists and the team behind managing it. From there, we’ll talk about what’s happened over the last few releases, Kubernetes 1.14 and Kubernetes 1.15, as well as some of what’s planned for Kubernetes 1.16. Additionally, we’ll cover some user stories of implementing Kubernetes on Azure. content.title: Intro: CNCF Serverless WG/CloudEvents
content.author: Scott Nichols
content.summary: An introductory session on the CNCF Serverless Working Group and the CloudEvents specification, covering the group's history, current status, a demo of CloudEvents, and future plans including the new Workflow sub‑group. This matters to Kubernetes users because serverless and event‑driven workloads are increasingly built on Kubernetes, and understanding CloudEvents enables consistent event handling across platforms.
content.description: This session will provide an introduction to the CNCF Serverless Working Group, the CloudEvents specification and the new Workflow sub-group. It will give an overview of our history, status of the work, demo of CloudEvents spec and future plans for the WG and CloudEvents project.

content.title: Intro: Helm
content.author: Michelle Noorali & Matt Fisher
content.summary: An introductory session on the CNCF Helm project, covering Helm's role as a package manager for Kubernetes, how to get started with Helm, and how to create and manage Charts for deploying applications.
content.description: In this session, we will introduce the basics of the CNCF Helm project. Helm is a Kubernetes package manager and it allows you to install and manages packages of Kubernetes configuration called Charts. Charts provide a way to deploy configurable, out-of-the-box applications and even package your own applications for Kubernetes. content.title: Intro: Kubernetes (Instrumentation) SIG
content.author: Frederic Branczyk
content.summary: An introductory maintainer‑track session that explains the role of SIG Instrumentation within Kubernetes, how to contribute, and reviews past and current work and sub‑projects.
content.description: The intro to SIG Instrumentation is going to be a lightweight introduction to what sig-instrumentation is responsible for within Kubernetes and give guidance on how to contribute to SIG Instrumentation. Beyond that it will cover a high level overview of the work SIG instrumentation has done over the years and elaborate on current efforts including the sub projects being worked on.

content.title: Intro: Linkerd
content.author: William Morgan
content.summary: An introductory session on Linkerd and the service mesh model, highlighting its benefits for observability, reliability, and security in Kubernetes environments, followed by lightning talks from production users and a Q&A.
content.description: In this session, William Morgan and Linkerd maintainers, will provide an introduction to Linkerd and the service mesh model. We'll hear some lightning talks from current Linkerd production users, and finish with a brief Q&A.

content.title: Intro: Network Service Mesh (NSM)
content.author: Frederick Kautz
content.summary: An introductory maintainer‑track session that explains how Network Service Mesh extends Kubernetes networking to support L2/L3 use cases such as VPN gateways, SR‑IOV NICs, and multi‑interface pods, offering a cloud‑native way to manage complex network requirements.
content.description: Network Service Mesh (NSM) is a novel approach solving L2/L3 network use cases in Kubernetes that are tricky to address with the existing Kubernetes Network Model. content.title: Intro: SPIFFE
content.author: Emiliano Bernbaum & Scott Emmons
content.summary: The session introduces SPIFFE and its implementation SPIRE, explaining how they provide a robust, cross‑environment authentication and trust framework for Kubernetes workloads, which is critical for securing modern microservice architectures.
content.description: Modern software development relies on many microservices working together, that in production may be distributed over different middleware systems, container schedulers, PaaS platforms and even different cloud providers. content.title: Kubernetes Failure Stories and How to Crash Your Clusters
content.author: Henning Jacobs
content.summary: Zalando shares its real‑world experience operating over 100 Kubernetes clusters on AWS, covering provisioning, incident response, and lessons learned from failures to help operators reduce unknown unknowns in production.
content.description: Bootstrapping a Kubernetes cluster is easy, rolling it out to nearly 200 engineering teams and operating it at scale is a challenge. In this talk, we are presenting our approach to Kubernetes provisioning on AWS, operations and developer experience for our growing Zalando developer base. We will walk you through our horror stories of operating 100+ clusters and share the insights we gained from incidents, failures, user reports and general observations. content.title: Benchmarking Cloud Native Storage
content.author: Josh Berkus
content.summary: The session presents a performance benchmark of various Kubernetes storage options—including host, network, cloud, and cloud‑native solutions like Rook—using workloads such as PostgreSQL and CockroachDB, helping operators understand trade‑offs in performance, reliability, and manageability for stateful applications.
content.description: You can run your stateful apps on Kubernetes. You can even run your databases on Kubernetes. But what are you giving up in performance? Is it worth it, or should you stick to the hosting you know? For the past several months, we've been benchmarking various forms of Kubernetes storage, including host storage, network storage, cloud storage and cloud-native storage systems like Rook. content.title: Kubernetes + Encrypted Memory = Security * Privacy
content.author: Harshal Patil & Pradipta Banerjee
content.summary: The session explores emerging hardware memory encryption technologies (Intel TME/MKTME, IBM Ultravisor) and demonstrates how the Kata container runtime was extended to secure Kubernetes Ephemeral (EmptyDir) volumes, ensuring data remains encrypted from the container image registry through runtime execution.

Once the hardware is out, it will change the way we perceive the security and privacy in the cloud. content.title: Istio New Workload Identity Provision Pipeline Based on Envoy SDS
content.author: Quanjie Lin & Diem Vu
content.summary: The session dives into Istio's new workload identity provisioning pipeline built on Envoy's Secret Discovery Service, covering its motivations, architecture, design decisions, CNCF project integrations, and real‑world enterprise deployments.
content.description: Istio introduces a new workload identity provision system based on envoy SDS (secret discovery service) from release-1.1; as the main developer who works on this project, my talk covers:1. Background topics like what is envoy SDS, the motivation why thenew system is introduced;2. High level end-to-end architecture, deep dive into some designdecisions we made during development;3. content.title: Meet the Ambassador
content.author: Alessandro Vozza
content.summary: An overview of the Kubernetes Ambassador program, highlighting the role of ambassadors in fostering community, supporting users, and promoting Kubernetes adoption, and why engagement with ambassadors matters for cluster operators and contributors.

content.title: Meet the Ambassador: Bob Killen, University of Michigan
content.summary: An introduction to Bob Killen, University of Michigan, highlighting his role as a Kubernetes ambassador and how community outreach and education drive the growth and health of the Kubernetes ecosystem.

content.title: Meet the Ambassador: Chris Hein, AWS
content.summary: This session introduces Chris Hein, an AWS Kubernetes ambassador, highlighting his role in the community and AWS's contributions to the Kubernetes ecosystem, helping users understand how the ambassador program supports collaboration and best practices on AWS managed services.

content.title: Meet the Maintainer: CNCF
content.author: Chris Aniszczyk
content.summary: A “Meet the Maintainer” session where CNCF’s Chris Aniszczyk discusses the CNCF’s role, governance, project incubation, and ways the community can get involved, helping Kubernetes users understand the broader cloud‑native ecosystem and contribution pathways.

content.title: Meet the Ambassador: Lachlan Evenson, Microsoft
content.summary: A conversational session with Microsoft’s Kubernetes community ambassador, Lachlan Evenson, discussing the role of ambassadors, Microsoft’s contributions to the Kubernetes ecosystem, and how users can engage with community and Azure Kubernetes Service.

content.title: Meet the Maintainer: CNCF
content.author: Chris Aniszczyk
content.summary: An overview of the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), its governance model, community initiatives, and how maintainers and ambassadors contribute to the Kubernetes ecosystem, helping users understand CNCF’s role and opportunities for involvement.

content.title: Meet the Ambassador: Lachlan Evenson, Microsoft
content.summary: In this Meet the Ambassador session, Microsoft’s Kubernetes ambassador Lachlan Evenson shares his experiences, community initiatives, and Microsoft’s contributions to the Kubernetes ecosystem, giving attendees insight into collaboration opportunities and the evolution of Azure’s Kubernetes offerings.

content.title: Meet The Maintainer: Open Policy Agent
content.author: Tim Hinrichs
content.summary: An introduction to the Open Policy Agent (OPA) project and its integration with Kubernetes via Gatekeeper, showing how policy-as-code can enforce security and operational rules across clusters, which is essential for compliance and consistent behavior.

content.title: Scavenging for Reusable Code in the Kubernetes Codebase
content.author: Kevin Lingerfelt
content.summary: Kevin Lingerfelt shows how Linkerd replaced custom implementations with reusable components from the Kubernetes codebase, such as shared informers and work queues, improving robustness and test coverage. The talk guides developers through a Go "scavenger hunt" to locate and apply Kubernetes internals, and discusses when to reuse existing code versus writing new implementations.
content.description: The magic of open source software and Go's support for remote import paths makes it trivial to import and run code from many of the most popular CNCF projects directly in your own project. Sometimes, however, the process of finding that one piece of code in a large codebase that’s just right for your use case can feel like a scavenger hunt. But the spoils of the hunt are vast. content.title: Kubernetes the New Research Platform
content.author: Lindsey Tulloch
content.summary: The session examines how academic research institutions are shifting from traditional batch jobs to diverse, dynamic workloads and how Kubernetes, aided by tools such as Argo, Kubeflow, and kube‑batch, provides an extensible platform to support these emerging research workflows.
content.description: Academic research institutions are at a precipice. They have historically been constrained to supporting classic “job” style workloads. With the growth of new workflow practices such as streaming data, science gateways, and more “dynamic” research using lambda-like functions, they must now support a variety of workloads. content.title: Kanary - Automated and Integrated Canary Testing Using CRD and an Operator
content.author: David Benque
content.summary: The session introduces Kanary, an operator and CRD that automates and integrates canary testing within Kubernetes, orchestrating traffic routing, validation, and rollout using Prometheus, Istio, and native resources.
content.description: The Kubernetes ecosystem provides primitives to easily deploy applications. Now, how might we simplify validation of a new application version before triggering its complete rollout? Canary testing is a popular answer. There are solutions to pilot canary testing from outside Kubernetes. How about driving it from inside Kubernetes instead? content.title: Intro: CLI SIG
content.author: Maciej Szulik
content.summary: An introductory session for the SIG CLI that walks new contributors through the kubectl code base, its development workflow, and the project's history, helping users and operators understand how to extend and improve the primary Kubernetes CLI tool.
content.description: This "intro" session will provide basic information to facilitate new SIG CLI contributors. This session will present an overview of the "kubectl" code base, as well as the basics of the development process. We will give a short history of this project. We will leave a significant amount of time for Q&A.

The session describes CoreDNS as the default DNS and its maturation, aligning with KEP-427 that graduates CoreDNS to GA, indicating the KEP's implementation details.

content.author: Daniel Garcia
content.summary: An introduction to CoreDNS covering its plugin-based architecture, role as the default Kubernetes DNS since 1.13, current roadmap, and practical Corefile examples for common use cases.
content.description: CoreDNS is a flexible and extensible DNS server with a focus on service discovery. Best known for its ability to serve as the cluster DNS of Kubernetes, CoreDNS is now the default DNS and part of the Kubernetes release since 1.13. The flexibility and extensibility of CoreDNS comes from its unique plugin-based architecture and its easy to use Corefile configurations. content.title: Intro: Fluentd
content.author: Masahiro Nakagawa
content.summary: The session introduces Fluentd, a flexible logging layer for cloud‑native environments, covering its administration and log processing concepts. It helps Kubernetes operators understand how to implement and extend logging solutions for reliable observability.
content.description: Logging for cloud-native applications and environments is a continuous challenge from an operational perspective. Fluentd offers a full logging layer than can be accommodated and extended as required to solve any logging need. In this Fluentd session, you will learn about its administration and log processing from a general perspective.

content.title: Intro: KubeEdge
content.author: Cindy Xing
content.summary: The session introduces KubeEdge, a CNCF sandbox project that enables managing edge nodes from the cloud and building IoT/edge infrastructure, discussing its design principles, challenges, and real‑world use cases.
content.description: Recently KubEdge was accepted as a CNCF sandbox project. As one of the reference architecture, KubeEdge provides customers a way to manage Edge nodes from cloud and build fundamental infrastructure targeted for IOT/Edge.Developers and end users can be empowered to build & run all kinds of potentials through KubeEdge. content.title: Intro: Kubernetes (VMware) SIG

links.reason: The session focuses on the vSphere CSI driver and explicitly discusses migration from the in‑tree vSphere storage plugin to CSI, which is the precise topic of KEP‑1491 (In‑tree Storage Plugin to CSI Migration – vSphere).

content.summary: This session introduces the vSphere CSI driver, demonstrating how to deploy, configure, and use it for persistent storage in Kubernetes on vSphere, and discusses migration from the in‑tree vSphere plugin, snapshots, and scheduling integration.

content.title: GPU Machine Learning From Laptop to Cloud
content.author: Mark Puddick
content.summary: The session demonstrates how to set up GPU‑accelerated containers for machine‑learning workloads on a local laptop and seamlessly migrate them to a cloud Kubernetes environment, enabling rapid iteration on small data sets and scaling to larger datasets. This is valuable for Kubernetes operators and developers who need practical patterns for packaging, deploying, and managing GPU workloads across hybrid environments.
content.description: In this session Mark will talk about how to setup and build containers to run GPU accelerated Machine Learning workloads on your laptop and move these easily to cloud. The session will cover setting up a local GPU accelerated environment, which can be great for testing on smaller data, then moving this over to run on larger sets in the cloud. Although the concepts in this session will focus on Python and Kersas workloads this can easily be applied to other machine learning technologies.

content.title: Deep Dive: CNCF CI
content.author: Lucina Stricko & Denver Williams
content.summary: The session explains how the CNCF CI dashboard (cncf.ci) provides third‑party validation of builds, deployments, and end‑to‑end tests for CNCF projects, focusing on ensuring Kubernetes and other projects run correctly on Arm and x86 architectures.
content.description: The CNCF CI status dashboard -- cncf.ci -- provides a third party validation of builds, deployments and end-to-end testing for CNCF’s Graduated and Incubating projects. CNCF welcomed Arm as Gold member in February 2019. The cncf.ci dashboard helps ensure that Kubernetes and other CNCF-hosted projects run well on Arm-based platforms. Attendees will leave this deep dive with an understanding of how the cncf.ci dashboard builds and tests projects on Arm and x86 architectures.

content.title: Deep Dive: CNCF Security SIG – Justin Cappos, New York University & Zhipeng Huang, Huawei
content.summary: The CNCF Security SIG deep‑dive explains the current state of cloud‑native authentication, authorization, auditing, policy enforcement, privacy and compliance, showcasing CNCF projects that help secure Kubernetes deployments.
content.description: CNCF Security SIG representing cross-cutting concerns including authentication, authorization, auditing, policy enforcement, privacy and compliance.  This session will present the state of cloud native authentication, authorization, policy controls and verification, highlighting CNCF projects that can help reduce risks for cloud native deployments and the ecosystem of tools and services.

content.title: Deep Dive: Kubernetes (Release) SIG

links.reason: The session describes the SIG Release's effort to create a unified, deterministic, reproducible build system for both development and official releases, which directly aligns with KEP-2420's goal of reducing Kubernetes build maintenance and improving build tooling.

Discussion of current build tooling, workflows, and future plans for a deterministic build system relates to KEP-2818's focus on reducing build maintenance in CI pipelines, involving build and CI improvements.

content.author: Tim Pepper & Stephen Augustus
content.summary: The session explores Kubernetes' Release Engineering SIG, detailing the history, current build tooling and workflows, and future plans for a unified, deterministic, and reproducible build system that serves both development and official releases.
content.description: Kubernetes is built through a motley collection of tools used in parallel and redundant ways on different cadences by a decentralized, global developer community. This runs counter to the established quality software engineering practice of a constantly exercised single build/test/release workflow. Our Release Engineering subproject aspires to a unified, deterministic, reproducible, verifiable build system used continually for dev/test as well as periodic official releases. content.title: Deep Dive: Open Policy Agent
content.author: Torin Sandall & Tim Hinrichs
content.summary: The session offers a quick overview of Open Policy Agent (OPA) followed by a deep dive into recent developments and future plans, illustrating how OPA can be leveraged for policy enforcement and admission control in Kubernetes. This matters to Kubernetes users and operators because it addresses security, compliance, and extensible governance across clusters.
content.description: Come to this session to hear from Tim Hinrichs and Torin Sandall, the co-creators of the OPA project. This session will provide a quick overview of OPA and then dive into recent developments and plans for the future. If you want to learn more about OPA or get involved, this session is for you!

content.title: Intro + Deep Dive: CNCF Storage WG
content.author: Alex Chircop
content.summary: An overview and deep dive into the CNCF Storage Working Group, covering storage technologies, architectural approaches, and findings from end‑user surveys to help Kubernetes users understand storage options and contribute to the community.
content.description: The CNCF Storage Working Group and SIG collaborates to explore and understandhow different storage technologies are used in cloud-native environments. Topics include block stores, file systems, object stores, key-value stores and databases, amongst others. Differentarchitectural approaches (centralized, distributed, sharded etc) are compared in terms of key attributes like availability, scalability, performance, data consistency, durability, fault tolerance, ease ofdevelopment and operational co

content.title: Intro: Auth SIG
content.author: Mo Khan
content.summary: An introductory overview of the Kubernetes SIG Authentication, covering recent achievements and short‑term goals to help newcomers understand how to contribute to the SIG and the upcoming work in upcoming releases.
content.description: We will present a high level overview of the SIG with an emphasis on recent accomplishments. Furthermore we will discuss immediate goals for the next few releases to help prospective individuals understand where they can get involved. This structure of presentation is similar to what we did in KubeCon NA 2018 - we received generally positive feedback from the community members.

content.title: Intro: Envoy
content.author: Lizan Zhou
content.summary: An introduction to Envoy, covering its high‑performance proxy architecture, extension points, and how to develop C++ or Lua extensions for network and HTTP filtering, which is essential for building and customizing service‑mesh solutions on Kubernetes.
content.description: Envoy is a high-performance proxy in the cloud-native landscape designed to be extensible at its core. There are several possible “extension points” in Envoy as outlined in https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/tree/master/source/extensions. However, the currently available approaches to extend it is rather limited. Since Envoy is written in C++, the primary way to introduce new extended functionality in Envoy is by writing an extension (e.g. filters, either network or HTTP filter, as one of the m

content.title: Intro: Vitess
content.author: Sugu Sougoumarane & Deepthi Sigireddi
content.summary: An overview of Vitess features followed by a hands‑on tutorial that shows how to deploy a Vitess cluster on Kubernetes, perform live traffic resharding, and leverage VReplication for real‑time sharded view materialization, enabling operators to run scalable MySQL workloads on K8s.
content.description: This session will cover a high level overview of all the Vitess features. Following this, we'll go over a tutorial on how to bring up a fully functional Vitess cluster in Kubernetes. Once up, we'll go through the steps to reshard the database while it's serving live traffic. Following this, we'll demonstrate the newest and most exciting feature of Vitess: VReplication, which allows you to materialize sharded views and rollups in real-time.

content.title: M3 and Prometheus, Monitoring at Planet Scale for Everyone
content.author: Rob Skillington
content.summary: This session explores how M3, an open‑source, highly scalable metrics platform, can be integrated with Prometheus to provide planet‑scale monitoring across multiple regions, using Kubernetes, Helm, and the M3 operator. It demonstrates deployment patterns and how to aggregate Prometheus data into a single global view.
content.description: For the past few years Prometheus has solved the monitoring needs of many and it is exceptional at what it does. Prometheus has exploded in popularity and now many wish to store more metrics, at longer retention and establish a single pane of glass on top of Prometheus for their monitoring needs across regions. M3 is an open source metrics platform that you can deploy and run using Kubernetes and Helm that integrates with Prometheus. It can store petabytes of metrics data with replication for hi

content.title: Restart-Free Vertical Scaling for Kubernetes Pods

links.reason: The session explicitly discusses a design for restart‑free vertical scaling of pod CPU and memory, which is exactly the feature described by KEP‑1287 (In‑place Update of Pod Resources) that enables in‑place pod resource changes without restarts.

content.author: Vinay Kulkarni
content.summary: The session presents a design for restart‑free vertical scaling of pod CPU and memory, detailing the Kubernetes component changes, scheduler race handling, disruption budgets, and failure retries, and showcases a real‑world gene‑sequencing use case.
content.description: Currently, vertical scaling of Kubernetes pod CPU or memory resources requires pod restarts. This is disruptive to services, and expensive for long-running applications or jobs. It is very important to have the ability to scale pod resources without restarts. In this talk, Vinay and Peng will present a design for restart-free scaling of pod resources, with container restart as a policy-controlled choice rather than a necessity. They will illustrate a customer use case, a gene-sequencing applicat

content.title: Zero Trust Service Mesh with Calico, SPIRE, and Envoy
content.author: Shaun Crampton
content.summary: The session demonstrates how to secure a service mesh using a Zero Trust model by integrating SPIRE for strong cryptographic identities and Calico for fine‑grained network policies, enhancing security for Kubernetes workloads.
content.description: The promise of a service mesh is to be able to delegate the hard networking problems to a uniform set of proxies and controllers. An extremely important networking problem is securing traffic within the mesh. Service meshes based on the Envoy proxy are very popular and there is a large diversity of implementations, including many home-grown solutions that focus on routing but may not include security. Shaun and Evan will demonstrate how to enhance your service mesh to follow the Zero Trust netwo

content.title: Accelerating the Journey of an AI Algorithm to Production with OpenFaaS
content.author: Joost Noppen
content.summary: This case‑study shows how BT leveraged OpenFaaS serverless functions to accelerate the path from AI research to production, cutting delivery time from years to two months and dramatically reducing risk and investment.
content.description: At BT it used to take us 2-3 years to get from a research idea to an AI algorithm that can be consumed by an end-user in production. We needed to reduce the risk and the investment required to bring our products to market and get essential feedback.We addressed three key areas to improve: having a diverse range of developer skills amongst us researchers, a lack of modern packaging & CI/CD practice, a need for a cloud-native model to shrink-wrap and run our code in production at scale.Our journey

content.title: JustFootball’s Journey to gRPC + Linkerd in Production
content.author: Ben Lambert
content.summary: The session details Just Football’s migration from HTTP/1.1 to HTTP/2/gRPC on Kubernetes and how they use Linkerd for observability and load‑balancing, sharing best practices for production gRPC services.
content.description: Ben (Just Football) will talk about their journey with Kubernetes and microservices from the world of HTTP/1.1 to HTTP/2.0 and gRPC. He will talk about the reasons for moving, and the best practices Just Football adopted for using gRPC in production, including monitoring + design decisions and distribution of gRPC proto + clients. Kevin (Buoyant) will cover how Linkerd provides Just Football with observability and load balancing for their gRPC services. He'll also describe how the Linkerd projec

content.title: Data Without Borders - Using Rook Storage Orchestration at a Global Scale
content.author: Jared Watts
content.summary: The session explores how the Rook project orchestrates storage systems across multiple Kubernetes clusters at global scale, covering replication, mirroring, snapshots, and disaster recovery to enable resilient, cloud‑native data services.
content.description: The Rook project has established robust and reliable patterns for orchestrating storage systems running on-top of Kubernetes clusters. However, storage systems often need to extend beyond a single cluster to provide data to end users in many different locations. How can these globally distributed storage systems best be orchestrated and managed to meet the needs of their users on a global scale? In this talk, we will examine the key concepts of storage orchestration for cloud native applications

content.title: Build a Kubernetes Based Cloud Native Storage Solution From Scratch
content.author: Sheng Yang
content.summary: The session shares a case-study of building Longhorn, a cloud‑native storage solution built from the ground up on Kubernetes, highlighting the use of Kubernetes controllers, workloads, and HA mechanisms to create a modern storage stack.
content.description: When it comes to cloud-native and container-ready storage, most industry discussions focus on how to make existing storage systems work with Kubernetes/Docker. But the rapid development of SSD technology, along with container and Kubernetes, make it possible to create a more elegant solution from scratch, compared to the storage technologies exist tens of years ago. So they have created a storage solution based on Kubernetes. In Longhorn, control flow is driven by Kubernetes's controller model;

content.title: Merging Quickly in a Cloud Native World
content.author: Lucas Roesler
content.summary: The talk walks through the Git workflow and contribution process for the OpenFaaS project, offering practical advice on how maintainers evaluate pull requests and how contributors can get their changes merged faster, which benefits the broader Kubernetes ecosystem.
content.description: You are really excited by a new project, you have a great idea to contribute, you click submit ... and wait. The latest StackOverflow community report states that 80% of surveyed developers are coding in their free time but only 44% are contributing to open source projects. While this number seems good, can we do better? How can we ensure that both contributors and maintainers enjoy and benefit from participating? In this presentation Lucas goes behind the scenes of the OpenFaaS project to share

links.reason: The session describes the planned In-Place Resources Update feature that allows modifying a Pod's CPU and memory requests/limits without killing the Pod. This directly corresponds to KEP-1287 "In-place Update of Pod Resources", which defines the Kubernetes implementation for in‑place pod resource resizing.

content.author: Karol Gołąb & Beata Skiba
content.summary: The session introduces the planned In-Place Resources Update feature, which lets you modify a Pod’s CPU and memory requests/limits on the fly without killing the Pod, eliminating disruption and improving cluster utilization.
content.description: Whether you’re using Vertical Pod Autoscaler or controlling Pod resources on your own, one thing is certain: applying new settings is disruptive as it requires Pods to be killed and recreated. Why should you change those setting you might ask? Stale settings, incompatible with your current load, might cause CPU starvation and Out Of Memory events or hinder cluster utilization. content.title: Towards Kubeflow 1.0, Bringing a Cloud Native Platform For ML to Kubernetes
content.author: David Aronchick
content.summary: The session presents the evolution of Kubeflow towards a 1.0 release, highlighting how it integrates cloud‑native technologies to provide a cohesive platform for the full machine‑learning lifecycle, including hyperparameter tuning with Katib and pipelines for orchestrating ML workflows.
content.description: In December of 2017, a small number of folks from a handful of companies introduced Kubeflow; an open, cloud native platform for machine learning. The project has gained a lot of momentum with hundreds of committers, thousands of commits and stars. With the traction, many companies are asking if can Kubeflow help them bring their ML practices to the next level, and where Kubeflow is going next. This talk will discuss the growth of the Kubeflow ecosystem and its place in the lifecycle of ML devel

content.title: Deep Dive: CNCF Serverless WG/CloudEvents
content.author: Clemens Vasters
content.summary: An in‑depth look at the CNCF Serverless Working Group, covering the CloudEvents spec and the newly formed Workflow sub‑group, discussing technical challenges and gathering community feedback.
content.description: This session will provide a more in-depth discussion of the Serverless working group, the CloudEvents specification and the new Workflow sub-group. It will include a more interactive discussion with the audience around some of the technical challenges we're facing and to solicit feedback as to the needs of the community.

content.title: Deep Dive: Falco
content.author: Michael Ducy
content.summary: The session explains how Falco can be extended to ingest Kubernetes audit events and custom application-level events, and how to author Falco rules for these streams, giving attendees deep insight into Falco’s architecture and its integration with Kubernetes.
content.description: In any Cloud Native architecture there’s a seemingly endless stream of events that happen at each layer. These events can be used to detect abnormal activity and possible security incidents, as well as providing an audit trail of activity. In this talk we’ll cover how we extended Falco to ingest events beyond just host system calls, such as Kubernetes audit events or even application level events. We will also show how to create Falco rules to detect behaviors in these new event streams. We show

content.title: Deep Dive: Kubernetes Architecture SIG

links.reason: The session explicitly covers the KEP process, API review process, and conformance testing review, which are core components of the Production Readiness Review Process defined in KEP-1194.
Discussion of conformance testing review aligns with KEP-1333, which ensures that conformance tests do not depend on beta APIs, a topic likely addressed in the session.

content.author: Timothy St. Clair
content.summary: A deep-dive into the SIG Architecture subprojects, covering the KEP process, API and conformance testing reviews, code organization, and project scope, to give attendees insight into Kubernetes architectural layering, governance, and future direction.
content.description: This will go into deep coverage of SIG Architecture's subprojects including the KEP process, the API review process, conformance testing review, and code organization. Other topics may include the evolving definition of what is in and out of scope for the project, as well as the latest visualizations of the ecosystem. Attendees should have a much better understanding of project architectural layering, governance, and goals.

content.title: Deep Dive: Network Service Mesh (NSM)
content.author: Nikolay Nikolaev
content.summary: The session provides a technical deep dive into Network Service Mesh (NSM), demonstrating how to integrate NSM for L2/L3 connectivity, adapt existing services without code changes, build new network services, and compose complex services—offering practical guidance and demos for Kubernetes operators and developers.
content.description: Network Service Mesh (NSM) is a young and ambitious project, offering solutions to many current problems around Cloud-Native Networking Connectivity in the L2/L3 layers. content.title: Deep Dive: Rook
content.author: Jared Watts & Bassam Tabbara
content.summary: A deep dive into Rook, the cloud‑native storage orchestrator for Kubernetes, covering its architecture, new storage provider integrations like Cassandra and EdgeFS, and how it enables dynamic provisioning of persistent resources for portable applications.
content.description: In this talk, we will be taking a deep-dive through both the architecture and some of the more recent developments of the Rook project. Rook is an open source cloud-native storage orchestrator for Kubernetes, providing the platform, framework, and support for a diverse set of storage solutions to natively integrate with cloud-native environments. We will learn in more depth about the recently added support for new storage providers, such as Cassandra and EdgeFS. We will also explore how Rook can

content.title: Intro: Brigade
content.author: Radu Matei
content.summary: An introduction to Brigade, a lightweight Kubernetes-native framework for building event‑driven workflows with JavaScript, showing how to get started, integrate GitHub, CloudEvents, and use cases ranging from security scanning to preview environments.
content.description: Brigade is a lightweight, Kubernetes-native framework which allows the creation of event-driven workflows. Using JavaScript, Brigade chains together containers and controls their execution in an in-cluster scripting environment that enables easy error handling and data sharing. In this session, you will learn how to get started with Brigade, how to use the existing GitHub, CloudEvents and generic event support and integrate them in your workflow, and how different companies are using Brigade to

content.title: Intro: Telepresence
content.author: Richard Li
content.summary: The session introduces Telepresence, a tool that streamlines Kubernetes development workflows by allowing developers to run local code within a cluster context, accelerating iteration cycles. It also covers Telepresence’s evolution from a VPN‑style proxy to a sophisticated L7 routing layer for developers.
content.description: We'll talk about development workflows for Kubernetes. We'll discuss the differences between traditional development, and different approaches people take to building Kubernetes services. We'll then introduce Telepresence and discuss how it integrates with different organizational development workflows. Finally, we'll talk about the evolution of Telepresence and how we are actively moving Telepresence forward from its heritage as a VPN-type approach into a more sophisticated L7 routing layer for

content.title: From New Cluster to Insight. Deploying Monitoring and Logging to Kubernetes
content.author: Eddie Zaneski
content.summary: The session shows how to quickly bootstrap observability on a fresh Kubernetes cluster using open‑source tools (Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Helm), providing a live deployment walkthrough and practical lessons from monitoring large workloads at DigitalOcean.
content.description: The question that most people ask after spinning up their first Kubernetes cluster is "how do I do monitoring and logging". In this session we'll utilize open source tools like Prometheus, Helm, Grafana, and Loki to quickly go from being in the dark to having full visibility into the happenings of our clusters and workloads. We'll deploy an entire monitoring and logging stack to a fresh cluster live and discuss the pros and cons of such tools. You'll leave this session with a playbook on how to

content.title: Koping with Change: What kops Learned Adopting etcd3, cluster-api and CRDs

links.reason: The session discusses migrating kops to etcd3, which directly involves changes to the Kubernetes etcd storage interface detailed in KEP-4743.
The session describes replacing an aggregated API server with CustomResourceDefinitions, a specific implementation change that aligns with the CRD graduation and usage defined in KEP-95.

content.author: Justin Santa Barbara
content.summary: This session details how the kops team tackled the rapid evolution of Kubernetes by migrating to etcd3, replacing an aggregated API server with CRDs, and adopting the Cluster API, sharing the operational challenges and strategies for reliable cluster management.
content.description: Kubernetes continues to adds features rapidly, but this makes it hard to install and operating a reliable kubernetes cluster. kops is an official OSS installation tool that makes kubernetes installation and operation turn-key. But doing that requires that kops manage that complexity. We’ve had a busy year, migrating to etcd3, moving from an aggregated-apiserver to CRDs, starting to adopt the cluster-api. content.title: Crafty Requests: Deep Dive Into Kubernetes CVE-2018-1002105
content.author: Ian Coldwater
content.summary: A technical deep dive into the severe CVE-2018-1002105 vulnerability, explaining how it exploits the kubelet API and permission model, and providing mitigation guidance for Kubernetes operators.
content.description: You may have heard about CVE-2018-1002105, one of the most severe Kubernetes security vulnerabilities of all time. But how does this flaw work? How can it be exploited, and what does it all mean? This deep dive will walk the audience through the Kubernetes back end, going over relevant concepts like aggregated API servers, the kubelet API, and permissions for namespace-constrained users. content.title: FaaS is Not Only the Serverless: Stream Processing with Serverless
content.author: Jun Makishi & Kensaku Komatsu
content.summary: The session introduces a novel serverless approach for long‑lived, stream‑processing functions on Kubernetes, enabling real‑time AI‑powered analytics by orchestrating multiple functions per data stream. It demonstrates a NTT Communications platform built with Kubernetes and gRPC, showcasing a live demo of voice streaming and media processing.
content.description: Function as a Service is the popular solution of Serverless, which runs a short-lived function. In contrast, we will show a new Serverless: run long-lived function to deal with stream data. Our proposal is unique since it starts multiple Serverless functions for single stream, and let them keep processing the stream one after another. content.title: Service Meshes: At What Cost?
content.author: Lee Calcote
content.summary: The session presents a methodology and results for measuring the performance overhead of service meshes, using a common benchmark tool across multiple meshes and proxies, helping operators understand the cost of adopting mesh technologies.
content.description: “What is the performance impact that a service mesh has?" "What overhead does being on the mesh incur?” By far, this is the most common questioned by engineers coming to with the value of functionality provided by a service mesh. Generally, this question goes unanswered. content.title: Benchmarking Cloud Native Databases Performance on Kubernetes
content.author: Iqbal Farabi & Tara Baskara
content.summary: The session presents benchmarking results for several cloud‑native databases (Vitess, CockroachDB, FoundationDB, TiDB, YugaByte) running on Kubernetes, focusing on their scalability and elasticity. It helps operators understand performance trade‑offs when deploying stateful workloads on K8s.

content.title: Meet The Maintainer: Harbor
content.author: Steven Ren
content.summary: This session introduces Harbor, the CNCF-hosted open‑source container registry, highlighting its capabilities for secure image storage, vulnerability scanning, and policy enforcement, which are critical for maintaining a trustworthy Kubernetes workload supply chain.

content.title: Meet The Maintainer: Rook
content.author: Jared Watts
content.summary: An overview of the Rook project, a cloud‑native storage orchestrator that simplifies deployment and management of storage solutions on Kubernetes, highlighting its role in providing CSI drivers, storage classes, and data services for stateful workloads.

content.title: Meet The Maintainer: Harbor
content.author: Michael Michael
content.summary: This session introduces Harbor, an open-source cloud‑native container registry that provides image storage, vulnerability scanning, and policy enforcement, helping Kubernetes operators secure and manage the container image supply chain.

content.title: Meet The Maintainer: Linkerd
content.author: Thomas Rampelberg
content.summary: A meetup with Linkerd maintainer Thomas Rampelberg, providing an overview of the Linkerd service mesh, its architecture, and why it matters for Kubernetes users seeking reliable, observable, and secure traffic management.

content.title: Meet The Maintainer: Open Policy Agent
content.author: Patrick East
content.summary: This session introduces the Open Policy Agent (OPA) project, its role in providing fine‑grained, policy‑as‑code enforcement for Kubernetes clusters, and why operators need it to improve security and compliance.

content.title: Meet The Maintainer: Vitess
content.author: Deepthi Sigireddi
content.summary: An overview of Vitess, the open‑source database clustering system for MySQL, presented by its maintainer. The talk explains how Vitess runs on Kubernetes, its architecture, and why it matters for operators needing scalable, highly‑available MySQL workloads.

content.title: Hacking Helm
content.author: Paul Czarkowski
content.summary: The session explores the security risks of Helm v2, especially the Tiller component, by demonstrating real-world hacks that can expose application information and compromise the cluster, and then shows how to mitigate these vulnerabilities.
content.description: Helm is the best way to build, package, and run Kubernetes manifests. However it has been considered by some as a fairly insecure way to deploy software, mostly due to its server component Tiller. content.title: 2 Years of TGIKubernetes
content.author: Joe Beda
content.summary: Joe Beda reflects on the two-year history of the TGIKubernetes series, sharing lessons learned about community-driven knowledge sharing and how open-source tooling can be iterated on quickly, highlighting its impact on the Kubernetes ecosystem.
content.description: 2 years ago Joe Beda tweeted about a Friday afternoon “Hacking on Kubernetes with Joe”. The overall interest with overwhelming. The sessions serve as an archive of Kubernetes and cloud native knowledge that we share with the broader open source community. What started out as a fun carefree afternoon with Joe, later turned into one of the most prized cloud native resources on the internet. content.title: Lifecycle of a kubectl Command: Harden Kubernetes Setup with Automation
content.author: Sanjary Rahman
content.summary: The session details how Booking.com automates the hardening of multi-tenant, on‑premise Kubernetes clusters using custom controllers, Pod Security Policies, and auth/admission webhooks, eliminating manual effort.
content.description: We at Booking.com run tens of on-premise multi-tenant Kubernetes clusters at scale. content.title: Building Cross-Cloud ML Pipelines with Kubeflow with Spark & Tensorflow
content.author: Holden Karau
content.summary: The session demonstrates how Kubeflow can orchestrate cross‑cloud machine‑learning pipelines using Spark and TensorFlow, showing how Kubernetes can replace YARN for data‑processing and model serving across multiple clouds.
content.description: Data Science, Machine Learning, and Artificial Intelligence has exploded in popularity in the last five years, but the nagging question remains, “How to put models into production?” In this talk, we present KubeFlow- an open source project aims to answer this. content.title: Deep Dive Fluent Bit: Logging & Stream Processing
content.author: Eduardo Silva
content.summary: This deep‑dive explores Fluent Bit’s architecture, data workflow, advanced transformation capabilities, and introduces edge stream‑processing, helping Kubernetes operators build efficient logging and real‑time data pipelines.
content.description: Fluent Bit is a Fluentd sub-project that aims to solve hard data challenges in the cloud space. On this deep dive session, we will talk about its architecture, how data workflows operate and the ability to perform advanced data transformation. Also, we will demonstrate the new ability to perform Stream Processing on the Edge.

content.title: Deep Dive: Contributor Experience SIG
content.author: Elsie Phillips
content.summary: This session provides a live look into the Contributor Experience SIG meetings, introducing the SIG’s role and showing how community members can get involved and contribute to Kubernetes.
content.description: Join us for a live session of the weekly contributor experience meeting! Meet members of the SIG in person and learn how you can contribute. Check out the agenda [here] (https://docs.google.com/document/d/1qf-02B7EOrItQgwXFxgqZ5qjW0mtfu5qkYIF1Hl4ZLI/edit)

links.reason: The SIG Instrumentation deep‑dive covers recent performance optimizations and how to leverage Kubernetes‑exposed telemetry for monitoring and alerting. KEP‑1206 (Kubernetes Metrics Overhaul) is the core KEP that implements a new metrics instrumentation framework in the control‑plane and kubelet, providing the telemetry referenced in the session.

content.summary: The session dives into recent performance optimizations in Kubernetes and demonstrates how to leverage the platform’s exposed telemetry for advanced monitoring and alerting, helping operators improve cluster efficiency and reliability.
content.description: The SIG Instrumentation deep dive is going to cover some of the details of performance optimizations we have recently been working on, both on a technical level of how they were achieved, but also the results of said optimizations. content.author: Jeremy Rickard
content.summary: The session dives into Virtual Kubelet’s core interfaces, showing how developers can create their first provider and highlighting contributions like Alibaba’s Elastic Container Instance provider, helping users extend Kubernetes with custom node implementations.
content.description: Virtual Kubelet has most recently been accepted into the CNCF as a sandboxed project. As the project continues to grow in contributors and users we are always looking for ways to educate folks on how to contribute back to Virtual Kubelet. In this talk we will focus on the core interface of Virtual Kubelet and how a developer could get started with building his/her first provider! content.title: Meet the Ambassador

content.summary: The session dives into Kubernetes' three standardized metric APIs, shows how to set up a Prometheus‑based metrics pipeline, and demonstrates using those APIs to drive Horizontal Pod Autoscaler scaling for Deployments with custom metrics.
content.description: Kubernetes traditionally uses metrics for its core scheduling decisions - in the beginning all of this started with an opinionated internal stack. Since then Kubernetes has introduced 3 orthogonal standardized metrics APIs. As of today many implementations exist - i.e. for cloud providers and on premise. content.title: The Magic of Kubernetes Self-Healing Capabilities
content.author: Saad Ali
content.summary: This session explains Kubernetes' self‑healing mechanisms, detailing how its declarative API and control loops continuously drive the cluster toward the desired state, with deep examples from the storage subsystem. It highlights current edge cases and upcoming improvements for operators managing large clusters.
content.description: Kubernetes is used to manage large-scale clusters with hundreds or thousands of nodes. Components will inevitably fail at this scale, but human intervention to detect and correct these failures is unsustainable. This is where Kubernetes shines. With a declarative API and guarantees of eventual consistency, Kubernetes is able to continuously monitor the system and take actions to keep the cluster healthy. This talk provides an architectural overview of the self-healing capabilities of Kubernetes.

content.title: Inside the CNCF Project Security Reviews
content.author: Justin Cormack
content.summary: The session explains the CNCF’s security review process for its projects, sharing findings, common vulnerabilities, and lessons learned to help Kubernetes users and operators understand project security posture and prepare for future reviews.
content.description: Last year the CNCF started funding security reviews for its projects. This talk examines the review process from the inside and looks at the outcomes and lessons from the reviews that have been performed so far. What vulnerabilities were found? What types of problem are common across projects? How should you prepare for a review? content.author: Stephan Fudeus & David Meder-Marouelli

content.title: Meet The Ambassador: Michael Mueller, Container Solutions
content.summary: An introductory session featuring Michael Mueller, a CNCF Ambassador from Container Solutions, that highlights the ambassador role, community engagement, and resources available for Kubernetes users and operators.

content.title: Strategies to "Kubernetify" Legacy Applications
content.author: Sai Vennam
content.summary: The session presents practical strategies for incrementally modernizing legacy applications on Kubernetes, focusing on maintaining agility, quality, and high‑availability while avoiding a risky full‑migration "big bang" approach.

This growth is supplemented by key technologies like Docker, Kubernetes, Istio and many more. content.author: Anu Engineer & Marton Elek
content.summary: This session presents a real‑world refactor of Apache Hadoop’s Ozone object store to run as a cloud‑native storage solution on Kubernetes, discussing the benefits of leveraging K8s for orchestration. This is a dialogue between two developers who are exploring and trying to finding the true path to becoming Cloud Native. content.title: 5 Steps to Building Inclusive Communities
content.author: Ashlynn Polini
content.summary: The session offers a practical 5‑step framework for creating inclusive, welcoming communities and events for developers and operators, helping Kubernetes users foster engagement and better user experiences.

content.title: Managing Machine Learning in Production with Kubeflow and DevOps
content.author: David Aronchick
content.summary: The session explains how to productize machine‑learning workloads on Kubernetes by combining Kubeflow with DevOps/GitOps practices, covering model reproducibility, versioning, validation, and safe deployment using an end‑to‑end Git‑driven workflow.
content.description: Kubeflow has helped bring machine learning to Kubernetes, but there’s still a significant gap relative to how to productize these workloads. links.reason: The session is a deep dive with the Kubernetes Multitenancy Working Group discussing current status and ongoing work. content.description: Kubernetes started as a general purpose orchestration framework with a focus on serving jobs. content.description: You may know DevStats as a repository of contributor statistics for Kubernetes (devstats.cncf.io), but you're about to find out that it is also a great demonstration case of migrating a complete application to orchestrated microservices. content.summary: This session dives into Cortex, a CNCF sandbox project that provides horizontally scalable, highly available, multi‑tenant long‑term storage and a Prometheus‑compatible query API. Unfortunately implementing effective and maintainable policies can be quite challenging.
